newsitem.title: USA: U.S. retailers urge Clinton to intervene in UPS.
newsitem.headline: U.S. retailers urge Clinton to intervene in UPS.

text.p: Chief executives of major retailers asked President Clinton Wednesday to intervene in the strike at United Parcel Service.

Members of the National Retail Federation released copies of a letter to Clinton urging him to personally encourage the company and representatives of the Teamsters union to return to the bargaining table.

The letter, signed by the chief executive officers of companies such as Sears, Kmart Corp, Federated Department Stores Inc, and Toy R US Inc, said the strike was having "profound economic consequences."
"Within the retail industry, the shipment of goods is our lifeblood," the letter said.
Approximately $50 billion of the nearly $2.5 trillion in annual retail sales was generated by catalog and mail-order sales, the letter said.
But that, it said, was a fraction of the untold billions of dollars in goods that were shipped to and from retailers every day of the week, creating jobs and generating tax revenue.
"The economy, which is enjoying unprecendented sustained growth, could experience a sudden downward spiral if this strike continues for an extended period." the retailers said.
